title: Privilege catalog
description: Formal shape of privilege-catalog.yaml — the named privileges an agent may be permitted to do (per COR-028). Each entry declares a recognizer (structured matcher over Bash commands and/or harness tool names, with a regex escape hatch) and an optional scope dimension. Namespace owner: permission-grants references entries via the typed token `[privilege-catalog:<id>]` (COR-019). Companion per COR-018 / the .pkit/schemas/ area conventions. An installed capability MAY ship a fragment of this same shape at `.pkit/capabilities/<cap>/permissions/privilege-catalog.yaml`, which the loader merges into the central catalog (the merge rule — additive, collision-rejecting, capability-scoped — is ADR-021's). Authoring constraints on a fragment: write keys as bare kebab-case ids (the loader applies the `<cap>:` scope), and `guardrail` and `locks` are forbidden in a fragment.

privileges.description: Privilege definitions. Keys are kebab-case ids; values match $defs.entry.

locks.description: The locked commands (ADR-095 point 3, ADR-099 point 1): the commands that change what judges every later call. The decision core gives a lock's verdict with no model, in every mode, on a shell call it reads as one of them; the adapter renders each as native rules beside it. Only the backbone's catalog declares a lock: the loader rejects a capability fragment's, as it rejects a guardrail.

description.description: What the locked command does, in words a reason can quote after `before`.

verdict.description: `ask`: the interlock's ask, in every mode. `deny`: denied outright, a person's gesture no agent's call makes.

line.description: For a deny, the command line the person runs from a terminal of their own, which the reason gives.

lock_matcher.description: One form of a locked command: `methodology`, the methodology command's leading words, read under `pkit` and through uv's runners; or `installer`, uv's group and subcommand, met where a word after the subcommand is one `word_any` names or a word of the call holds a package name `text_any` names (with neither, every call of the subcommand meets it).

privilege_ref.description: Narrowed cross-schema reference pattern for the privilege-catalog namespace (per COR-019). Consumers $ref this rather than redeclaring the pattern. The id half MAY carry a capability scope (`<cap>:<name>`, e.g. `[privilege-catalog:trip-planning:ad-hoc-scraping]`) for a capability-contributed privilege per ADR-021 — the COR-019 token-grammar clarification.

bash_matcher.description: One Bash-command recognizer. Either a structured matcher (cmd [+ subcommand] [+ flag_any] [+ word_prefix_any]) or a regex escape hatch (pattern). The runtime matcher segments compound commands and strips env-var prefixes before matching. For a deny, the decision core also reads a structured matcher's program, subcommand and flags in the forms programs read them (ADR-025 point 5), and a pattern's flags as written.

subcommand.description: If present, the first non-flag token after `cmd` must be one of these (e.g. `[run, exec]` to match `docker run` but not `docker ps`).

flag_any.description: If present, the command must carry at least one of these flags (e.g. `[-rf, -fr]` for a destructive-rm guardrail).

word_prefix_any.description: If present, a word after `cmd` must open with one of these (e.g. `[+]` for a git refspec that forces the update of its ref).

pattern.description: Regex escape hatch matched against a command segment when the structured fields can't express the case. The author owns its fragility (Q4c).

description.description: One-line, domain-readable description of what this privilege permits.

recognize.description: How a request is identified as this privilege. At least one of `bash` / `tool` / `path`.

path.description: A path-scoped allow: the privilege is recognized only for a file tool listed in `tools` whose target lies inside one of `folders` — never for the tool alone, and never for a shell command, which is judged like any other — so a grant of it neither reaches nor denies anything elsewhere. It reduces prompts; it confines nothing. Enforced by the hook, which sees the target; never realized as a session-wide rule. The agent workspace (#1043) is the shipped instance.

folders.description: Folders relative to the root of a checkout of the project — the project root, or another working tree of its repository, each with its own copy of the folder. No leading `/` or `~`, no `..`; a folder reached through a symlink is never recognized.

tools.description: File tools recognized when the path they name lies inside a folder (e.g. `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`).

bash.description: Bash-command recognizers; a request matches if any item matches a command segment.

tool.description: Harness tool names this privilege covers (e.g. `Read`, `WebFetch`).

scope_type.description: The scope dimension a grant of this privilege may constrain. `directory` = path globs (enforced per-call by the hook); `domain` = host allowlist. Absent = unscoped (anywhere).

guardrail.description: If true, the model synthesizes a baseline `{subject: all, effect: deny}` grant for this privilege — the catalog is the single source of truth for the guardrail deny set (per ADR-002's double-lock). The synthesized model deny is the fail-open hook half; the harness's native settings denies are the fail-closed half. Absent = false.
